title: Facilitator Guide: 180-Minute Workshop for Adoption Evaluation

facilitator-s000.title: Before You Begin
facilitator-s000.markdown: This guide proposes a workshop format for 10–20 workshop participants to evaluate the value of Fabric Planning and the conditions for adoption through hands-on experience. The focus is not on introducing every feature, but on **deciding which planning process to try first in your organization**. The schedule and staffing are recommendations for this workshop, not Microsoft product requirements.

facilitator-s001.title: HTML for Projection / Distribution
facilitator-s001.markdown:
**Distribute only the [participant HTML](workshop-presentation.html) to participants.** It contains the procedures for Labs 00–09, knowledge checks, and safety notes, but not the answers or instructor facilitation materials.

Instructors use the [instructor HTML](workshop-instructor.html). In addition to the same exercises, it includes the answers and this guide's preparation, schedule, prompts, recovery steps, and cost review. Do not distribute the instructor HTML to participants. This separates the distributed content; it is not access control for the repository's Markdown files.

Both files are standalone HTML documents with Japanese / English language switching. Download the required file and open it in Edge / Chrome. Use the table of contents to move to the day's scope, the arrows to advance through the steps, and select an image to enlarge it. Regenerate both files before distribution and run the synchronization check. [Usage / update guide](PRESENTATION-GUIDE-JA.md)

HTML progress indicates the viewing position, not completion of hands-on work by participants. Offline viewing does not replace authentication / capacity / billing conditions. The HTML includes all workshop materials, including Labs 07 / 09, but does not automatically add them to the 180-minute schedule below.

facilitator-s002.title: What Participants Should Take Away
facilitator-s002.markdown:
The goal is for participants to be able to explain these four points:

1. Which handoffs can be reduced by allocating company-wide targets and connecting field input with approval.
2. How to distinguish actuals, plans, and forecasts, and where an input change is reflected.
3. How a plan saved to Fabric SQL can be used in downstream analysis.
4. Whether they can identify the process, data, stakeholders, success criteria, and cost-review owner for a trial in their organization.

facilitator-s003.title: Recommended Facilitation Format
facilitator-s003.markdown:
**The default format is for the instructor to handle design and configuration while participants experience input / review / approval.** Asking everyone to create items from the start increases the burden of permissions, time, and billing. If learning how to create items is an objective, schedule a separate implementation-focused exercise.

For 10 participants, form 5 pairs; for 20, form 10 pairs. One person operates while the other checks the assumptions behind the numbers, then they switch. Each person must use their own account to sign in and enter data; do not share accounts. As a guide, staff a 10-person session with one instructor and one assistant, and a 20-person session with one instructor and two assistants.

For a two-stage approval exercise, assign one person in each pair as the requester and the other as the regional approver, with the instructor acting as headquarters approver. Keep the request-status column separate from the two approval columns for regional and headquarters approval, and rehearse in advance with three distinct IDs. If the pair alone tests requesting and approving, clearly describe it as a one-stage approval exercise. Follow the [Lab02 setup and checks](../labs/02-allocation-and-collaboration.md#パート4承認を依頼する), and record only the scope actually completed, including notifications.

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Instructor / FP&A lead | Overall targets, design demonstration, approval explanation, and timekeeping |
| Participant / regional owner | Enter plans for assigned regions / products, comment on assumptions, and check the results of changes |
| Participant / reviewer | Record figures before and after input, and explain the difference between the target and the field forecast |
| Assistant instructor | Triage sign-in, connection, and permission issues, and help participants who fall behind recover |

Do not have everyone edit the same cell at the same time. Assign each pair a region / product / time slot. Explain that these operational assignments to avoid conflicts in a shared sheet are distinct from security-based access control.

**In an input-focused session, participants do not perform every step in the original labs.** The instructor prepares the planning sheets, input columns, forecasts, and scenarios, and configures the design and locks, writeback target, and other settings in advance; explain these through demonstrations on the day. Participants enter data in prepared leaf cells, add comments, approve, and check results. Only the instructor changes company-wide totals, performs top-down allocation, changes locks, or runs Optimizer; other participants do not enter data during those activities. If you change the format so everyone operates the design, revise the cost and schedule assumptions to reflect Planner usage.

facilitator-s004.title: One Week Before: Check with the Administrator and Verify the Environment
facilitator-s004.markdown:
- Follow [Module 00](../labs/00-prerequisites.md) to check capacity, tenant settings, model Read / Build permissions, sharing for the Plan item, and writeback permissions.
- If you will run Module 09 as a separate session, confirm with the administrator the capacity requirements (paid F2 or higher, or P1 with Fabric enabled), Data Agent / Tenant AI settings, cross-geo processing policy, and availability of Ontology Preview. Prepare a Snapshot in advance to compare the Forecast from Lab04 with model values; do not infer that an unverified writeback history is "latest." In hands-on testing of the sample route, Entra pass-through without a CREDENTIAL clause was used when copying a CSV from Lakehouse Files to a Warehouse, while the route specifying Workspace Identity failed. Do not treat Workspace Identity as a requirement; use only authentication / permissions approved by your organization.
- If using B2B guests, test sign-in through data entry with the actual participant IDs. Do not use a check with internal accounts for everyone as a substitute for testing guest access.
- For the person setting up the exercise, use Member / Admin in the exercise workspace by default, and limit participant permissions to those needed for their tasks. Billing roles are distinct from workspace role names and vary by operation.
- Official materials include both an explanation that metadata is stored in SQL and an explanation that new Plans are stored in OneLake. Check what is available when creating a new Plan in the actual environment; do not require everyone to follow steps for an older screen.
- Inventory the trial capacity's database limits, existing item count, number of planning sheets, and planned SQL writeback targets. Do not delete items to free capacity when it is unclear whether they are unnecessary.
- Do not use a production workspace, customer data, or real operational approval routes.

facilitator-s005.title: 2–3 Days Before: Rehearse the Full Workshop
facilitator-s005.markdown:
- Prepare the same sample as this workshop and complete [01](../labs/01-environment-and-first-sheet.md) → [02](../labs/02-allocation-and-collaboration.md) → [03](../labs/03-optimizer.md) → [04](../labs/04-forecast-and-writeback.md) → [06](../labs/06-intelligence-canvas.md).
- Record the UI names, target model, date hierarchy, and value display units in the actual screens. If the Japanese UI labels differ, provide participants with a mapping to the English identifiers used in the materials.
- Prepare these recovery checkpoints: A: model connected; B: allocation and input columns ready; C: forecast created; D: writeback and live KPI verified. Check whether the preparation method is officially supported; do not assume that duplication carries over connections, approvals, or writeback settings.
- Use a separate participant ID to check viewing, input, approval, and writeback. Also confirm that rows or actions are not visible to users who lack permission.
- Check Capacity Metrics and SQL consumption, and test with the expected number of participants. Do not present F2 as the recommended capacity for that group size.
- Prepare the instructor's screen and the saved values, logs, and screenshots for a successful run. If you switch to recording or screen sharing, do not count that as completion of participant operations.

facilitator-s006.title: The Day Before / Immediately Before the Session
facilitator-s006.markdown:
- Tell participants how to check sign-in, which browser and exercise URL to use, how data will be handled, and which tenant bears the cost.
- Give the assistant instructors the pair numbers and their areas of responsibility. Do not have all participants troubleshoot a connection error at once; have an assistant instructor triage it.
- Confirm with the responsible owner which actions start a billable session and that it cannot be ended partway through. Do not tell participants that deleting items or stopping capacity after the exercise removes the session charge.

facilitator-s007.title: Day-of Schedule: 180 Minutes Total
facilitator-s007.markdown:
| Elapsed | Duration | Content | What participants check |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 0–10 min | 10 min | Share the challenge and goals | Name one aggregation or adjustment problem in their organization |
| 10–25 min | 15 min | 00 / 01: Key points on permissions and billing, and check the prepared environment | Open the model and sheet with the designated account |
| 25–35 min | 10 min | 01: Review the current state in the existing report | Distinguish FY25 actuals from the FY26 target |
| 35–60 min | 25 min | 02: Allocation, field input, comments / approval | The total after allocation matches the target, and locked values do not change |
| 60–75 min | 15 min | 03: Instructor Optimizer demo + pair review | Decide whether inputs that meet the target are operationally sound |
| 75–85 min | 10 min | Break | Assistant instructors check for anyone falling behind |
| 85–110 min | 25 min | 04: Forecast and writeback | Compare the success log with SQL values |
| 110–130 min | 20 min | 06: Link input and canvas | A change to one cell is reflected in the corresponding live KPI |
| 130–145 min | 15 min | 08: Capacity / governance | Adapt the discussion to their organization's participant count, operations, and permissions |
| 145–160 min | 15 min | Complete the adoption evaluation worksheet | Decide the PoC scope, owners, and success criteria |
| 160–180 min | 20 min | Questions, recovery, and wrap-up buffer | Record unresolved items with an owner and due date |

This schedule does not allow time for everyone to create the full environment on the day. Cover the details of measures / row models in 05, PowerTable in 07, Cube, and Infobridge in an advanced session or a short instructor demonstration, depending on the objective. In particular, do not use the unresolved P&L aggregation in 05 as a success criterion for the customer-facing main session.

facilitator-s008.title: Advanced Session: Module 09 (Add 45–60 Minutes)
facilitator-s008.markdown:
Module 09 is a **separate session, not part of the existing 180-minute main workshop**. The HTML covers Parts 3–5 starting from the synthetic CSV. Use the Warehouse for explicit-type staging and independent numerical verification, and bind Ontology / Graph to the Lakehouse managed Delta table. Check row counts / keys / values before configuring Ontology Preview and the read-only Fabric Data Agent. The 45–60-minute estimate does not include data preparation. Agent Q1 / Q3 / Q4c have been verified against synthetic values, but Q4 / Q4a returned `SQLCandidatesFailedFilterError`. See [Lab09](../labs/09-variance-analyst.md) for the scope of hands-on verification.





Entry conditions are paid F2 or higher, or P1 with Fabric enabled; administrator-approved Tenant AI / cross-geo settings; availability of Ontology Preview; billing approval for a dedicated Warehouse / Lakehouse Files; and the runner's approved read path and required read permissions for the Plan / model. Do not treat Workspace Identity as a requirement; even the demonstrated Entra pass-through without a CREDENTIAL clause may be used only when organizational policy and permissions allow it. Do not begin if you cannot establish the complete current state of Long with Changes; prepare an approved full Snapshot instead. Do not call Northwind's Open period values confirmed actuals, and independently compare Agent answers with full-precision Warehouse values. The Agent cannot change, approve, or write back to the Plan.

Use [Module 09](../labs/09-variance-analyst.md) for the procedures, data contract, verification, and safe shutdown. If running this with participants, do not include tenant-specific information or data rows in public displays or recordings, and do not substitute permission checks for each participant with results from an administrator account.

facilitator-s009.title: Questions That Connect the Experience to Adoption Decisions
facilitator-s009.markdown:
| Experience | Instructor prompt | Follow-up to take away |
|---|---|---|
| Allocation / locks | “Where do you allocate target changes while protecting months that are already finalized?” | Allocation criteria, lock granularity, exception handling |
| Comments / approval | “How do you currently find the assumptions behind this number and who approved it last?” | Requirements for submitters, approvers, and evidence |
| Optimizer | “Are there combinations that meet the target but cannot be executed?” | Constraints, adjustable drivers, and human final judgment |
| Statistical forecast | “What do you compare against to check whether a forecast is reasonable before adopting it?” | History period, seasonality, error, explainability |
| Writeback | “Which reports or business processes should receive an approved plan?” | Destination, refresh frequency, granularity, permissions |
| Live KPI | “Who checks the impact of a change without confusing actuals with plans?” | Measure source, display units, and how changes reach the model |

Do not claim that the sample operations alone demonstrate time savings or return on investment. Ask about the customer's current measures and make them topics to measure in a PoC.

facilitator-s010.title: Success Criteria and How to Recover When Things Go Wrong
facilitator-s010.markdown:
| Situation | Success criteria | If not met |
|---|---|---|
| Connection | Data from the specified model is displayed | Assistant instructor checks the ID, Read / Build, and tenant settings. Participants continue in the prepared environment or follow the instructor demonstration. |
| Allocation | The total matches the target and the locked period is unchanged | Check the target cells, measures, hierarchy, and locks. Record the current values before trying again. |
| Optimization | Explain the target and result, constraints, and inputs that changed | Do not hide mismatched numbers; check the constraints and acceptable error. |
| Writeback | The success log for the current run matches the target scenario, rows, and values in SQL | Preserve errors or partial states. A row count alone is not success. Check permissions, destination, format, and NULL values. |
| Canvas | Changing the target input changes the KPI that references From Sheets | Check whether a model-derived measure is being used. Do not claim that values in the source model also change. |
| Data separation | Confirm both allowed and denied access with a different user | Check legacy access control, Roles & Policies, model RLS, and SQL connection IDs separately. |

If a problem occurs, record the starting value, target sheet / scenario, action, expected value, actual result, and log timestamp. After a fix, repeat the same operation and, if possible, have another person verify it.

facilitator-s011.title: Cost Review for 10–20 Participants
facilitator-s011.markdown:
The estimates below use the official per-session figures of **847 / 168 / 37 CU-hours for Planner / Stakeholder / Viewer**. They assume that everyone starts a new session, uses the same tenant and capacity, and that **one instructor in addition to the participants is a Planner**. They exclude assistant instructors, SQL, OneLake, automation, Infobridge, and other costs. This table does not guarantee a monetary amount or required SKU.

| Format | 10 participants + 1 instructor | 20 participants + 1 instructor |
|---|---:|---:|
| Everyone creates planning sheets (everyone is a Planner) | 9,317 CU-hours | 17,787 CU-hours |
| Instructor creates; participants enter data / approve (Stakeholder) | 2,527 CU-hours | 4,207 CU-hours |
| Instructor demonstrates; participants sign in individually and view only (Viewer) | 1,217 CU-hours | 1,587 CU-hours |

The formula is `847 + 参加者数 × 各ロールの消費量`. Even when participants take turns in pairs, the role is determined by the operations performed with each person's account. Creating sheets or changing the design partway through may result in an upgrade to a higher role. Check the session's validity scope, upgrade behavior, and remaining duration in the [official billing documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/plan/resources/billing-fabric-plan) and [role descriptions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/plan/overview-roles).

The official billing example says "30 days (730 hours)." Thirty calendar days is 720 hours, but this guide does not replace the official calculation assumptions. Check the actual expiration and billing in the admin interface. Do not estimate the experience for 20 people or total cost from the smallest capacity for the product.

facilitator-s012.title: Adoption Evaluation Worksheet
facilitator-s012.markdown:
During the 15-minute period from 145–160 minutes, each organization selects one item to evaluate.

| Item | What to record |
|---|---|
| First process to try | For example, monthly sales forecast or departmental expense budget. Focus on one for this exercise. |
| Current challenge | A specific situation, such as waiting for aggregation, inconsistent figures, or identifying an approver |
| Current measure and success criteria | Current close duration, number of manual operations, time spent checking variances. What will be measured at the end of the PoC? |
| Required data | Semantic model, periods, granularity, master data, and confidentiality classification |
| Stakeholders | Business owner, submitters, approvers, Fabric administrator, and security contact |
| Conditions to validate | Connection, permissions, RLS, writeback, capacity, operations, and availability in the target region |
| Next step | PoC scope, owner, schedule, and the person responsible for cost review |

After the workshop, share observed successes and unmet criteria separately from the scope completed and items to check next time. Customer communication, scheduling, and environment changes must stay within the scope agreed by the responsible people at each organization.
